terms.comment: Distinguish labrum, lip, with a short a.

phrases.latin: Post cēnam pater, epitoniō versō, solium aquā calidā implēvit … In solium Theodōrus dēscendēns «Aquam calidam amō,» inquit, «sīcut Rōmānī!»
phrases.english: After supper Dad turned on the tap and filled the bath with hot water … Climbing into the bath, Theo said, “I love hot water, like the Romans!”
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: Lewis & Short: solium · Lewis & Short: labrum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 122.
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
